sanskrit: ayaṃ me varaṇa urasi rājā devo vanaspatiḥ | sa me kṣatraṃ ca rāṣṭraṃ ca paśūn ojaś ca me dadhat ||
english: This varaṇa upon my chest — king, god, lord of the forest — may he bestow on me sovereignty, dominion, cattle, and vital force.

sanskrit: imaṃ bibharmi varaṇam āyuṣmāñ chataśāradaḥ | sa me śatrūn vi bādhatām indro dasyūn ivāsurān ||
english: I bear this varaṇa, possessing life, one of a hundred autumns; may he drive away my enemies even as Indra drives the Dasyus like Asuras.

sanskrit: yathā vāto vanaspatīn jīrṇān bhanakty ojasā | evā sapatnāṃs tvaṃ bhaṅdhi pūrvāñ jātān utāparān varaṇas tvābhi rakṣatu ||
english: As the wind breaks aged forest trees with its might, so do thou shatter my rivals — those born before and those born after; may Varaṇa protect thee on all sides.

sanskrit: yathā vātena prakṣīṇā vṛkṣāḥ śere nyarpitāḥ | (evā sapatnāṃs) tvaṃ sarvān pra kṣiṇīhi nyarpaya pūrvāñ jātān utāparān varaṇas (tvābhi rakṣatu) ||
english: As trees withered by the wind lie cast down and felled, so do thou utterly destroy and lay low all my rivals — those born before and those born after; may Varaṇa protect thee.

sanskrit: yathā vātaś cāgniś ca sarvān psāto vanaspatīn | evā sapatnāṃs tvaṃ psāhi pūrvāñ jātān utāparān varaṇas tvābhi rakṣatu ||
english: As the wind and fire together consume all forest trees, so do thou consume all my rivals — those born before and those born after; may Varaṇa protect thee on all sides.

sanskrit: tāṃs tvaṃ pra chindhi varaṇa purā diṣṭāt purāyuṣaḥ | ya imaṃ paśuṣu dipsanti ye cāsya rāṣṭradipsavaḥ ||
english: Do thou cut them off, O Varaṇa, before their appointed doom, before their full lifespan — those who seek to harm him among his cattle, and those who seek to harm his realm.

sanskrit: yathā sūryo atibhāti yathāsmin teja āhitam | evā sapatnāṃs tvaṃ sarvān ati bhāhi śvaḥśvo varaṇas tvābhi rakṣatu ||
english: As the sun shines pre-eminent, as splendor is established in him, so do thou outshine all my rivals day by day; may Varaṇa protect thee on all sides.

sanskrit: yathā yaśaḥ pṛthivyāṃ yathāsmiñ jātavedasi | evā me varaṇo maṇiḥ kīrtiṃ bhūtiṃ ni yacchatu tejasā mā sam ukṣatu yaśasā sam anaktu mām ||
english: As glory abides in the earth, as glory abides in Jātavedas — so may my varaṇa amulet confer on me fame and prosperity; may it anoint me with its brilliance, anoint me with its glory.

sanskrit: yathā yaśo agnihotre vaṣaṭkāre yathā yaśaḥ | (…) ||
english: As glory resides in the Agnihotra, as glory resides in the vaṣaṭ-call — [so may my varaṇa amulet confer on me fame and prosperity; may it anoint me with its brilliance, anoint me with its glory].

sanskrit: yathā yaśaḥ somapīthe madhuparke yathā yaśaḥ | (…) ||
english: As glory resides in the soma-drinking, as glory resides in the honey-mixture — [so may my varaṇa amulet confer on me fame and prosperity; may it anoint me with its brilliance, anoint me with its glory].

sanskrit: yathā yaśaḥ kanyāyāṃ yathāsmin saṃbhṛte rathe | (…) ||
english: As glory resides in a maiden, as glory resides in this fully equipped chariot — [so may my varaṇa amulet confer on me fame and prosperity; may it anoint me with its brilliance, anoint me with its glory].

sanskrit: yathā yaśaś candramasy āditye ca nṛcakṣasi | (…) ||
english: As glory resides in the moon and in Āditya the all-seeing eye of men — [so may my varaṇa amulet confer on me fame and prosperity; may it anoint me with its brilliance, anoint me with its glory].

sanskrit: yathā yaśaḥ prajāpatau yathāsmin parameṣṭhini | (…) ||
english: As glory resides in Prajāpati, as glory resides in Parameṣṭhin — [so may my varaṇa amulet confer on me fame and prosperity; may it anoint me with its brilliance, anoint me with its glory].

sanskrit: yathā deveṣv amṛtaṃ yathaiṣu satyam āhitam | evā me varaṇo maṇiḥ kīrtiṃ bhūtiṃ ni yacchatu tejasā mā sam ukṣatu yaśasā sam anaktu mām ||
english: As immortality is established among the gods, as truth is established among them — so may my varaṇa amulet confer on me fame and prosperity; may it anoint me with its brilliance, anoint me with its glory.

sanskrit: asya vāmasya palitasya hotus tasya bhrātā madhyamo asty aśnaḥ | tṛtīyo bhrātā ghṛtapṛṣṭho asya- -atrāpaśyaṃ viśpatiṃ saptaputram ||
english: Of this brilliant, hoary Hotṛ — his middle brother is the devourer of food; the third brother is he of butter-bright back. Here I beheld the lord of the people who has seven sons.

sanskrit: sapta yuñjanti ratham ekacakram eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā | trinābhi cakram ajaram anarvaṃ yasminn imā viśvā bhuvanāni tasthuḥ ||
english: Seven harness the one-wheeled chariot; one horse bearing seven names draws it. The three-naveled wheel is unaging and unchecked; upon it all these worlds are established.

sanskrit: imā ratham adhi ye sapta tasthuḥ saptacakraṃ sapta vahanty aśvāḥ | sapta svāsaro abhi saṃ navanta yatra gavāṃ nihitā sapta nāmā ||
english: Those seven who stand upon this chariot, the seven-wheeled — seven horses draw it; seven sisters sing forth together where the seven names of the cows are hidden.

sanskrit: ko dadarśa prathamaṃ jāyamānam asthanvantaṃ yad anasthā bibharti | bhūmyā asur asṛg ātmā kva svit ko vidvāṃsam upa gāt praṣṭum etat ||
english: Who perceived it first at its birth — the bone-possessing one that the boneless one bears? The breath of life, the blood, the self of the earth — where indeed is it? Who has gone to a knower to ask this?

sanskrit: pākaḥ pṛcchāmi manasāvijānan devānām enā nihitā padāni | vatse baṣkaye 'dhi sapta tantūn vi tatnire kavaya otavā u ||
english: Unwise, I ask with my mind not understanding — the hidden footprints of the gods lie in this. Upon the young calf the seers have spread seven threads, which are to be woven.

sanskrit: acikitvāṃś cikituṣaś cid atra kavīn pṛcchāmi vidmane na vidvān | vi yas tastambha ṣaḍ imā rajāṃsy ajasya rūpe kim api svid ekam ||
english: Unknowing yet questioning even the knowing seers here, I ask for understanding though I understand not — who propped apart these six expanses in the form of the unborn? What is that one thing?

sanskrit: iha bravītu ya īm aṅga veda- -asya vāmasya nihitaṃ padaṃ veḥ | śīrṣṇaḥ kṣīraṃ duhrate gāvo asya vavriṃ vasānā udakaṃ padāpuḥ ||
english: Let him declare here who truly knows it — the hidden track of this lovely bird. The cows milk milk from his head; clad in a covering they have fetched water with their feet.

sanskrit: mātā pitaram ṛta ā babhāja dhīty agre manasā saṃ hi jagme | sā bībhatsur garbharasā nividdhā namasvanta id upavākam īyuḥ ||
english: The mother has embraced the father in truth; at the beginning she met him in thought, with mind. She, the shuddering womb-fluid, was buried within; reverencing, they approached to invoke her.

sanskrit: yuktā mātāsīd dhuri dakṣiṇāyā atiṣṭhad garbho vṛjanīṣv antaḥ | amīmed vatso anu gām apaśyad viśvarūpyaṃ triṣu yojaneṣu ||
english: Yoked, the mother stood at the right-side pole; the embryo stood within the enclosures. The calf lowed, looking after the cow, the all-formed one, in the three journeys.

sanskrit: tisro mātṝs trīn pitṝn bibhrad eka ūrdhvas tasthau nem ava glāpayanti | mantrayante divo amuṣya pṛṣṭhe viśvavidaṃ vācam aviśvaminvām ||
english: Bearing three mothers and three fathers, one stood erect; they do not wear him down. On the back of yonder sky they deliberate — an all-knowing speech that does not fill all.
